blocks.text: Understanding public enterprises and cooperatives is crucial for grasping how businesses operate in Nigeria.

blocks.markdown: Public enterprises are businesses owned and operated by the government. They are established to provide essential services and goods that may not be profitable for private enterprises. Examples in Nigeria include the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) and the Nigerian Railway Corporation.

blocks.title: What are Public Enterprises?
blocks.text: Public enterprises are government-owned businesses aimed at providing services to the public and promoting economic development.

blocks.markdown: Privatisation refers to the transfer of ownership of a public enterprise to private individuals or organizations. This process is often undertaken to improve efficiency and profitability. Commercialisation, on the other hand, involves making a public enterprise operate more like a private business, focusing on profit-making while still being owned by the government.

blocks.title: Understanding Privatisation and Commercialisation
blocks.prompt: Explain the difference between privatisation and commercialisation in the context of Nigerian public enterprises.

steps.text: Privatisation involves selling government-owned businesses to private investors.
Commercialisation focuses on enhancing the efficiency of public enterprises without changing their ownership.

blocks.answer: Privatisation transfers ownership to the private sector, while commercialisation retains government ownership but aims for profit-oriented operations.

blocks.markdown: Cooperative societies are organizations owned and operated by a group of individuals for their mutual benefit. They are characterized by democratic control, where each member has an equal say in decision-making. Types of cooperative societies in Nigeria include consumer cooperatives, agricultural cooperatives, and credit unions.

blocks.title: Features of Cooperative Societies
blocks.text: Cooperative societies are characterized by voluntary membership, democratic control, and profit-sharing among members.

points: Public enterprises are essential for providing services that may not be profitable for private businesses.
Privatisation and commercialisation are strategies to enhance the efficiency of public enterprises.
Cooperative societies promote mutual benefit and are governed democratically.
